item.content:encoded: Aljamain Sterling at UFC 300 | Photo: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Kshitiz Kumar Singh Aljamain Sterling’s move to featherweight has had its ups and downs, starting with a dominant win over Calvin Kattar, then a razor-close decision loss to Mosvar Evloev. He then bounced back with wins over Brian Ortega and Youssef Zalal, and just had a very close fight with 24-year-old contender Kevin Vallejos. At UFC Qatar , Sterling and Vallejos stifled each other’s best abilities, leading to a very contested fight round after round. The matchup between Sterling and Vallejos was extremely technical. The former bantamweight champion struggled to work in grappling and find openings, while Vallejos struggled to employ his game plan of keeping pressure and finding the knockout shot. The scorecards favored Vallejos’ action, with two judges giving him the win 30-27 and one 29-28. What does Aljamain Sterling think of the scoring in his UFC Qatar fight? Reflecting on the matchup during The Ariel Helwani Show , Aljamain Sterling said, “I’m not calling it a robbery. I just wish we could get some explanation on what they’re actually scoring.” Sterling went into detail on his questions about scoring criteria: “I know the criteria is damage, but what is damage when you’re being outstruck, and what’s damage when a guy is swinging and missing and not landing anything of significance.” Aljamain Sterling proposes a change to how fights are judged: “When the scorecards came, I thought it was going to go my way, and then when it didn’t, I was in disbelief. I was baffled. I don’t know what we’re scoring. I don’t know what scores anymore. I still think judges should be in the back room watching the fights. Why not? If you wanna progress the sport, you can’t keep changing the rules from week to week, where one thing happens, you score it this way, and then the next week you see something else scored a different way.” — Ariel Helwani (@arielhelwani) November 23, 2026 Sterling went on to give Vallejos a lot of credit, calling him the most dangerous 145-pounder. Vallejos has been on a tear in his recent fights, securing knockouts and Performance of the Night bonuses against both Giga Chikadze and Josh Emmett. Vallejos is a Contender Series alumni and his only loss of his career came against Jean Silva in their Contender Series matchup back in 2023. ALSO READ: What’s Next for Navajo Stirling After Knocking Out Jiri Prochazka at UFC Qatar? However, Sterling was able to stay at distance and did not take too many clean shots, so he does have valid questions about the scoring criteria, especially since he did narrowly outstrike the young contender in the first two rounds, went 1-14 on takedowns, and had 3:32 seconds of control time throughout the fight. While Vallejos did keep pressure on and had arguably the cleaner, more damaging strikes, Sterling still did great defensively and had the striking numbers. Ajlamain Sterling explains why he should have won his UFC Qatar fight Sterling explained his fighting style and how he viewed the matchup. He said, “I’m not the most powerful puncher. I can be honest with that, but I do know I can hit a lot of volume, I can make you work, and I can outpace you, and look for the finish that way. I think styles like mine almost get penalized, because we’re not that one hitter quitter type of fighter, and not looking to swing haymakers the whole time in a barnfight.” The former UFC champion added, “So I feel like that should have been enough to get the job done. Just based on the criteria, every single round I outstruck him, even off my back I outstruck him, and somehow I still managed to come up short.” Sterling also explained why he believes fighters should receive more detailed explanations of judging decisions. According to him, understanding what swayed the judges would help competitors adjust their game plans and focus on the factors that matter most when scoring rounds. Such a change could give fighters greater clarity on how to approach future matchups. However, the Unified Rules of MMA, developed with contributions from legendary referee “Big John” McCarthy , already outline the scoring criteria used by judges. For now, there appears to be little indication that the system will change in the way Sterling is proposing. Nevertheless, MMA continues to evolve, leaving room for potential changes in the future. Game planning remains crucial in high-stakes matchups, where both fighters bring significant strengths and a single mistake can prove costly. While Sterling would welcome greater transparency from judges, he has consistently demonstrated an ability to prepare effectively for opponents. His technical approach, high-volume striking, and ability to dictate the pace have helped him win rounds and find success against some of the toughest competition in the sport. item.title: Nvidia's position as cornerstone of AI trade confirmed by market reaction to Huang's return
item.description: Tech shares in Asia and Europe rebounded on Tuesday, following in the footsteps of Nvidia's shares closing on Wall Street 31 percent higher on Monday. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . After 11 months of international competition, the Davis Cup is officially down to the Final 8. One more week of matchups will determine the tournament's 2026 champions. Often referred to as the 'World Cup of Tennis', the Davis Cup features men's teams from across 150 countries, creating the largest annual team competition in the sport. The Cup began in 1900 as a singular match between the United States and Great Britain, and has since evolved into an international affair each year. The Final 8 is set to take place in Bologna, Italy this week, using a single-day, best-of-three knockout format. Three-time defending champions Italy will be chasing a fourth consecutive title, but without star Jannik Sinner. Carlos Alcaraz will be leading Spain's team, while Alexander Zverev represents Germany. Which nation will lift the Davis Cup trophy? item.title: Rob Gronkowski is ‘a little worried’ about the Jacksonville Jaguars after what he’s noticed
item.description: Photo by Paras Griffin/Getty Images Rob Gronkowski has suggested that the Jacksonville Jaguars are starting to make him a ‘little worried’ due to their inconsistency, which he thinks was on display against the New York Giants in Week 11. The Jaguars managed just 18 points against the Giants, their lowest points total since mid-September when they were beaten 20-13 by the Denver Broncos. Despite the recent 23-18 loss to the Giants, the Jags are still comfortably top of the AFC South and look pretty nailed on for a playoff berth. However, Gronkowski is worried that Jacksonville use up all their ‘greatness’ in the regular season and then struggle in the playoffs. Rob Gronkowski suggests Jaguars are too inconsistent during playoffs Speaking to NFL on Fox , he said: “I am a little worried about the Jags because of their inconsistency. They kind of showed and displayed this last year. Yeah, they’ve got a great team and they can show greatness at times, but then they hit the playoffs, the last couple of years, and boom, they just unload in a terrible way. It’s like they unload all their greatness.” Talking specifically about the Week 11 loss, he added: “It’s like they’ve used it all up throughout the whole season, and now they’re already showing periods like this game and moments where they’re just not showing up. They’ve got to show up on a consistent basis. “It’s not like, ‘Hey, you know, the playoffs are kicking in. We’re going to dominate now. We’re going to play our best football’. You’ve got to continue to play your best football throughout the whole year, especially against solid opponents. “Like the New York Giants. Yes, they shocked everyone, but they’re a solid team. Harbaugh is a great coach, you know? They’ve got McCarthy now. They’re playing together as a team. They want to win. It’s like there are no individuals. “Everyone’s in it together with the New York Giants. I’m not saying the Jags aren’t. I mean, I feel like there aren’t any individuals on that team, but they’re just too inconsistent over the years.” The Jaguars made it to the Wild Card Playoffs in 2025, losing 27-24 against the Buffalo Bills and you could make a case that their inconsistency was on display then. Trevor Lawrence is one of the top quarterbacks in the NFL but against the Bills, he threw a game-losing interception in the final few minutes, which cost his side. Prior to that, they competed in the 2022/23 season playoffs and were bested by the Kansas City Chiefs when Nick Bolton and Jaylen Watson capitalised on fumbles and interceptions in the fourth quarter to help their team win 27-20. It does feel like the Jaguars are never really blown away when they are beaten in the postseason. Instead, individual errors or lapses in concentration seem to be what costs them. But it’s hard to predict if that will change in 2026/27, as apart from the Giants’ loss, they have looked like one of the most complete teams in the regular campaign. item.title: Temi Nkem’s Oversized Braided Updo Is the Hairstyle Inspiration We Needed
item.description: Big Brother Naija 2026 winner Temi Nkem pairs a structured matte-gold leather corset and black velvet skirt with an architectural braided updo. If your next braid appointment has you thinking beyond the usual ponytail or bun, Temi Nkem has an idea you might want to take to your hairstylist. The Big Brother Naija 2026 winner wore her thick braids in a high, sculptural updo, with oversized loops arranged into a crown. She paired it with a gold-and-black look, complete with metallic beauty details and contrasting textures. Rather than letting her thick braids fall down her back, Temi has gathered them into a sleek, high updo, building them into an oversized crown of interlocking loops. The result is sculptural, full of volume and beautifully structured. It’s also a great example of how to style thick braids when you want a fresh way to wear them for an event. Pulling the hair up keeps the face open, while the loops create plenty of interest around the crown. And with the base kept sleek, the hairstyle gets to take centre stage without feeling too busy. Temi Nkem accents her sleek looped braid updo with metallic gold-leaf detailing, brow crystal, and glossy nude lips. Then there are the beauty details. Temi goes for smoky brown eyeshadow, full lashes and a glossy nude lip outlined in brown, keeping the makeup warm and complementary to the outfit. A little gold takes things further: there’s a tiny cross-shaped crystal between her brows, three vertical micro-beads on her chin, hammered circular gold earrings and flecks of metallic gold leaf tracing the side of her face, from her left temple down to her collarbone. It’s an unexpected beauty detail, and one that ties in beautifully with the colours of her outfit. Temi Nkem shows how to style thick braids into a sculptural crown paired with a gold-and-black corset gown. Now, about that gown! Temi shows how to wear gold and black with ease, starting with a structured matte-gold leather corset bodice. It features vertical seam boning, a deep V-plunge neckline and a sharply defined V-shaped basque waist. Below it, a fitted black velvet skirt brings a different texture into the look, while matching off-the-shoulder velvet arm bands complete the silhouette. The contrast between the gold leather and plush black velvet is what makes the combination work so well. Rather than having both colours compete for attention, the matte gold adds warmth and the black velvet gives the outfit balance. So, if thick braids are next on your salon mood board, you might want to save Temi’s updo. And if you’re planning a gold-and-black outfit, her mix of leather and velvet is another styling idea worth keeping. item.title: Buffalo Bills did something ‘incredible’ with Josh Allen to ‘unleash’ him against the Chiefs
item.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images The Thanksgiving game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Buffalo Bills is the marquee fixture, and the latter have done something ‘incredible’ with Josh Allen to prepare him for it. When the Kansas City Chiefs take on the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night, it will be a clash between two marquee quarterbacks and two winning teams. Patrick Mahomes is not surrendering his position and Josh Allen is coming for it, while this could easily be the Super Bowl game this season. To prepare Allen for this game in the best possible way, the Bills did something ‘incredible’ during their recent game against the Dolphins. Josh Allen protected against the Dolphins The Bills faced no issues dispatching the Dolphins in their recent game to go 9-1 this season and cement themselves as the best team in the NFL. Allen managed to gain 304 yards with his passing, completing 27/45 attempts, but it was a sloppy game by his usually world-class standards. NFL reporter Jordan Schultz, speaking on Ryan Clarke’s The Pivot podcast, said that Allen’s game was by design, as the Bills prioritised protecting him at all costs. Schultz said that for the first time ever, Allen took no part in any rushes, design runs, or scrambles, and that was all intentional. He said: “Something happened Sunday against Miami. And I’m looking at it right now. This is pretty incredible because I want to make sure I get this right. Josh Allen, this is the first time we’ve ever seen this in his career. He finished the game with zero rushing attempts. “No design runs, no scrambles, nothing. Everything went through the passing game or the running backs. And my understanding is that this was very strictly and deliberately by design. Buffalo wanted to make sure that Josh was fresh for Thursday, when the entire playbook will be available and he’ll be fully unleashed.” It is no surprise to see the Bills preparing this way for a game that could go a long way towards solidifying their championship prospects and placing Allen as the MVP favourite. Allen is now well-rested and safe to play to his full strengths in a game that will be watched and analysed by millions, and the Bills’ gamble will be spoken about as genius if they win that game after winning against the Dolphins as well. item.title: Champions League: Arsenal face tough Dortmund test as Man City welcome Napoli
item.description: Arsenal will face a stern test when they host Borussia Dortmund in the UEFA Champions League on Tuesday, while Manchester City welcome Italian champions Napoli to the Etihad Stadium as the competition enters Matchday Five. The two fixtures headline Tuesday’s European action, with both Premier League sides seeking important victories to strengthen their positions in the league phase. Arsenal, who currently occupy third position with 10 points from four matches, will be looking to maintain their impressive European run when they welcome Dortmund to the Emirates Stadium. Mikel Arteta’s side have recorded three victories and a draw in their opening four Champions League matches, beating Napoli, Lille and Slavia Prague before playing out a 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich. The Gunners, however, will be without goalkeeper David Raya, who sustained a shoulder injury during their recent encounter with Newcastle United. Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are also listed among their unavailable players ahead of the Dortmund clash. Dortmund, meanwhile, arrive in London in good form after moving to the top of the Bundesliga with a 1-0 victory over Borussia Monchengladbach at the weekend. The German side have also won three of their four Champions League matches, beating Real Betis, Sabah and Villarreal, although they suffered a 1-0 defeat to Bodo/Glimt. They currently sit one point behind Arsenal and will be hoping to close the gap with a positive result in London. The encounter will also offer an interesting reunion for Arsenal youngster Ethan Nwaneri, who is spending the season on loan at Dortmund and is eligible to feature against his parent club. Meanwhile, Manchester City will welcome Napoli in another important encounter at the Etihad Stadium. Enzo Maresca’s side occupy seventh position with nine points, while Napoli are 27th with three points after winning just one of their opening four matches. City head into the fixture after a 1-1 draw against Fulham in the Premier League, having struggled for consistency in recent domestic outings. They will, however, take confidence from their 3-2 victory over RB Leipzig in their previous Champions League fixture as they look to strengthen their chances of securing automatic qualification for the round of 16. City will be without Antoine Semenyo, who is sidelined with a knee injury, while Matheus Nunes remains a doubt. For Napoli, the trip to Manchester presents an opportunity to revive their European campaign after defeats to Arsenal, Villarreal and Porto. The Italian side secured a 1-0 victory over Torino in Serie A at the weekend but face a difficult assignment against Guardiola’s men. Former Manchester City midfielder Kevin De Bruyne is expected to feature for Napoli, adding another interesting storyline to the encounter. item.title: Bayern score ‘own goal’ as Musiala firestorm builds
item.description: Already ravaged by injuries, Bayern Munich head to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday swept up in a firestorm of their own making over star midfielder Jamal Musiala. Currently 13th in the table, Bayern need points if they are to reach the top eight and avoid a punishing extra knockout round. While Lille are languishing in 35th spot, last season’s semi-finalists Bayern limp into the clash despite being one of the leading contenders. Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was the latest to join Bayern’s bulging casualty ward with an ankle injury on Friday which will likely rule him out until February. But while Musiala returned after a two-month absence in last week’s match, club bosses were accused of launching a coordinated effort to pressure the midfielder into accepting a pay cut. That the club decided to kick-start the furore a day before announcing record revenues of close to a billion euros has not gone unnoticed. – ‘Own goal’ – In August, Musiala revealed he was suffering from a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”, having collapsed twice on the field in pre-season. After his return, club powerbroker Karl-Heinz Rummenigge told German TV the 23-year-old midfielder was unlikely to recapture his previous form due to the condition — and should consider taking a pay cut. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable,” Rummenigge told Sky Germany. Rummenigge’s statements were striking but echoed those made by former president and fellow powerbroker Uli Hoeness, along with current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen. item.dc:creator: Ayobami
item.content:encoded: Already ravaged by injuries, Bayern Munich head to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday swept up in a firestorm of their own making over star midfielder Jamal Musiala. Currently 13th in the table, Bayern need points if they are to reach the top eight and avoid a punishing extra knockout round. While Lille are languishing in 35th spot, last season’s semi-finalists Bayern limp into the clash despite being one of the leading contenders. Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane was the latest to join Bayern’s bulging casualty ward with an ankle injury on Friday which will likely rule him out until February. But while Musiala returned after a two-month absence in last week’s match, club bosses were accused of launching a coordinated effort to pressure the midfielder into accepting a pay cut. That the club decided to kick-start the furore a day before announcing record revenues of close to a billion euros has not gone unnoticed. – ‘Own goal’ – In August, Musiala revealed he was suffering from a “neurological disorder” which can lead to “temporary but treatable seizures”, having collapsed twice on the field in pre-season. After his return, club powerbroker Karl-Heinz Rummenigge told German TV the 23-year-old midfielder was unlikely to recapture his previous form due to the condition — and should consider taking a pay cut. “If he doesn’t return to being the Jamal of old, then we need to have a conversation with his family, with the player, and, above all, with his agency — because, frankly, the current financial figures would no longer be justifiable,” Rummenigge told Sky Germany. Rummenigge’s statements were striking but echoed those made by former president and fellow powerbroker Uli Hoeness, along with current CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen. On Sunday, player union FIFPRO slammed Bayern, accusing the club of a “coordinated campaign to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives” to accept a wage cut. “A club of Bayern’s standing should know better,” FIFPRO said in a statement. FIFPRO’s German counterparts VDV joined the chorus on Monday, saying the comments would “leave a lasting impression” on Musiala and on the club in general. “I believe those in charge have scored a real ‘own goal’ here,” VDV president Carsten Ramelow said in a statement. World Cup and Ballon d’Or winner Lothar Matthaeus, who has never been afraid to butt heads with Hoeness and the Bayern brass, said the club should provide Musiala with “every bit of support.” “Right now, everything is being placed on Musiala’s shoulders,” Matthaeus told RTL. “Perhaps all parties can sit down and talk later at a more opportune moment,” he added. – An opportunity for Musiala – For their part, Bayern coach Vincent Kompany and powerful sporting director Max Eberl have thrown their support behind Musiala publicly. Kompany, who himself returned on Friday from a month out after being hospitalised with meningeal irritation in October, backed Musiala. “The coach must be the one to believe in the player. And if we manage to bring him back, then everyone wins: the club, the fans — and all of German football.” Eberl said on Friday he was confident Musiala would return to his best form if given the chance. Bayern’s injury crisis has provided Musiala with an opportunity to illustrate his importance to the club by starring in the coming months. Besides Kane, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer will miss Wednesday’s match. Michael Olise and Luis Diaz are also injury doubts, meaning the only recognised fit forward is 18-year-old winger Lennart Karl. Musiala has not addressed the controversy directly, but gave an insight into how he shuts out pressure and critique at a fan event this weekend. Asked by a fan how he handled the weight of expectation, Musiala said he was still in the process of finding the right approach. “I’m still learning… Too much pressure isn’t good, but a hunger for victory is important,” Musiala said. “Finding that balance is a very important part of life.” The post Bayern score ‘own goal’ as Musiala firestorm builds appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 3 biggest takeaways for Sixers following home loss to Trail Blazers
item.description: PHILADELPHIA -- The Philadelphia 76ers played host to the Portland Trail Blazers on Monday night looking to keep things moving in the right direction. Unfortunately, a lack of size and 3-point production did them in as the Sixers fell to the Blazers 128-111 to fall to 14-4 on the season. LeBron James had 23 points, six rebounds, and three assists for Philadelphia while Brown had 20 points in his return from a hamstring strain. Tyrese Maxey had 22 points and five assists, VJ Edgecombe had 12 points, seven assists, and seven rebounds, and Jabari Walker had 10 points and five rebounds. Here are the three biggest takeaways for the Sixers following the loss: Lack of size in the paint This one can be filed under the "Well, duh" category, but without Joel Embiid, who was sidelined with an illness, it was a struggle for the Sixers against a taller Trail Blazers team. Portland won the rebounding battle 49-33 led by Donovan Clingan's 18 rebounds and the Blazers were able to have a ton of success on the offensive end due to the size advantage. One has to give Walker credit for giving it his all. It was obvious that he was ready to battle and do what he had to do, but he can't help the size mismatch with Clingan and Co. in Portland. "I think the biggest challenge is just how much help you can provide," Walker said after the loss. "Sometimes when the guards get downhill, it makes you question whether you can help and then get back. So that’s always in your mind when a guy like that is on the floor." Brown's foul trouble Brown looked phenomenal to start the night as he scored 19 points on 8-for-10 shooting in the first half as Philadelphia was able to keep up with Portland. However, Brown picked up his fourth foul early in the third quarter and had to sit the rest of the third, returned in the fourth, and just could not find his rhythm again. He only scored one point on 0-for-4 shooting and he knocked down a free-throw in the second half for his only offensive contributions. The 5-time All-Star was able to give Philadelphia an offensive threat, but the foul trouble really slowed him after halftime as the Trail Blazers took control. "I wasn't too happy about it," Brown said. "It’s over with now. I think that affected the game. It also affected my rhythm a little bit in the second half. I sit the whole third quarter and coming back off injury, coming back from hamstring. Just my body didn't really feel the same after that." The 3-point discrepancy Another big issue was the 3-point difference for both teams. The Sixers shot 9-for-33 from deep while the Blazers knocked down 19 on 42 attempts on the night. That 30-point difference is tough to make up for anybody, but especially for a Sixers team that had to play small with Embiid sidelined. Philadelphia not only couldn't make up for the rebounding and paint differences, but it also couldn't figure out the 3-point line either. "I wasn't too happy about it," Brown said. "It’s over with now. I think that affected the game. It also affected my rhythm a little bit in the second half. I sit the whole third quarter and coming back off injury, coming back from hamstring. Just my body didn't really feel the same after that." The 3-point discrepancy Another big issue was the 3-point difference for both teams. The Sixers shot 9-for-33 from deep while the Blazers knocked down 19 on 42 attempts on the night. Philadelphia not only couldn't make up for the rebounding and paint differences, but it also couldn't figure out the 3-point line either. Afterward, coach Nick Nurse stated: Well, I think that first of all, they outplayed us. Their energy and just hustle in general was excellent throughout the game. But the big thing is the three-point shooting, I think. It's hard to lose by 10 on that particular stat. Ten makes, that's 30 points. That's hard to overcome unless you're going to beat them at the free throw line extensively, or else you're going to win the turnover battle extensively as well. But possession battle was pretty even. And then they make 10 more 3s than you. And it's too bad, too, because I think we go 0-for-4 with Jabari, Dean (Wade), KCP (Kentavious Caldwell-Pope). And I think other than one of those, they were all great shots. Maybe one of KCP's, he had to arc it a little higher over Clingan coming out at him. But other than that, I think they were really good shots. So, would have liked to defensive rebound a little bit better. We got our share of them, too. Second chance points weren't too big of a difference really, but the three-point shooting was. item.title: Kolo Toure: ‘De Bruyne didn’t want to leave City, McTominay has been a surprise’
item.description: Kolo Toure: ‘De Bruyne didn’t want to leave City, McTominay has been a surprise’ Former Manchester City defender and assistant coach Kolo Toure says that Kevin De Bruyne never wanted to leave the Premier League side and says that he will want to show the fans that he is still at the top of his game when he returns to the Etihad Stadium on Tuesday night, and admits that Scott McTominay’s form in Serie A has been a surprise. The Ivorian, who served as an assistant to Pep Guardiola at City last season and was also part of Roberto Mancini’s Premier League winning squad in 2011-12, spoke to La Gazzetta dello Sport ahead of the meeting between Napoli and Manchester City in the Champions League on Tuesday night. NEWCASTLE UPON TYNE, ENGLAND – JANUARY 13: Manchester City assistant manager Kolo Toure looks on during the Carabao Cup Semi Final First Leg match between Newcastle United and Manchester City at St James’ Park on January 13, 2026 in Newcastle upon Tyne, England. (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images) Napoli head to the Etihad under pressure in the Champions League with just three points to their name from their first four matches of the competition in 2026-27, leaving them at risk of missing out on qualification for the knock-out rounds. There will be returns to Manchester for a number of Napoli players, including Man City legend De Bruyne, as well as former Manchester United stars McTominay and Rasmus Hojlund, all expected to start on the night. Toure on Man City vs. Napoli, De Bruyne and McTominay Asked how he sees Tuesday night’s game going, Toure told La Gazzetta dello Sport: “City will try to control the game and crush Napoli, and I think Allegri will set up with a compact team, careful in defence but ready to explode on the counter-attack, which could be dangerous. City will have to avoid those.” MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – SEPTEMBER 18: Jeremy Doku of Manchester City scores his team’s second goal past Vanja Milinkovic-Savic of Napoli during the UEFA Champions League 2025/26 League Phase MD1 match between Manchester City and SSC Napoli at City of Manchester Stadium on September 18, 2025 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Dan Istitene/Getty Images) Asked what City can do to prevent being hit on the counter, Toure said: “Two ways. The first is to start by pressing opponents immediately after losing the ball. The second is to have players fast enough on the pitch to get back into defensive positions once the counter-attack starts.” Toure was asked for his thoughts on De Bruyne. The Belgian superstar is into the final year of his contract with Napoli and there have been reports that he could look to leave as early as January. “Kevin was one of the best players in the history of the Premier League,” said Toure. “He is an incredible player, but more than anything, a great person. For me, what counts in football is what you do on the pitch, but what you do off it is also extremely important. Kevin is a champion in that respect. DE BRUYNE, ITALY – NOVEMBE

City will have to avoid those.” MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – SEPTEMBER 18: Jeremy Doku of Manchester City scores his team’s second goal past Vanja Milinkovic-Savic of Napoli during the UEFA Champions League 2025/26 League Phase MD1 match between Manchester City and SSC Napoli at City of Manchester Stadium on September 18, 2025 in Manchester, England. For me, what counts in football is what you do on the pitch, but what you do off it is also extremely important. Kevin is a champion in that respect. DE BRUYNE, ITALY – NOVEMBER 01: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli is challenged by Weston McKennie of Juventus during the Serie A match between Juventus and SSC Napoli at Allianz Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images) “I know he didn’t want to leave City. I think he will want to show that he should have stated. I’m sure he wants to make a difference for Napoli, but also to show the fans who still love him that he’s still the top player he was at City.” Toure admitted that it has been a ‘surprise’ to see quite how much McTominay has kicked on since moving to Serie A. “Honestly, yes [it has been a surprise]. But I listened to a podcast that he was on not too long ago and it became clear to me that he is a fighter, and that he’s very strong and intelligent. NAPLES, ITALY – NOVEMBER 21: Scott McTominay of SSC Napoli celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Torino FC at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on November 21, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) “He’s always been good physically, but he didn’t show enough of his technical qualities in the Premier League. He’s pulled them out in Italy and has also added the finishing touches in the final third. For me, he will be Napoli’s key player.” Asked for his predictions for Man City’s player of the match, Toure replied: “Enzo Fernandez. He’s in great form and is making the difference in midfield. Just like Haaland in attack.” Toure was then asked where he thinks the differences lie between Man City under Pep Guardiola last season and City under Maresca in 2026-26. He replied: “When you change coach, especially one of Guardiola’s calibre, for me, the best there has ever been, it’s always a challenge. City have also lost key players like Bernardo Silva, like Rodri, the best midfielder in the role. And leaders like Stones and Ake. “I think City did a great job in bringing in strong players like Fernandez and Bouaddi. Maresca needs time, but I’m sure they’ll find a way.” MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 17: Enzo Maresca, Manager of Manchester City, looks on before the Premier League 2026/27 match between Manchester City and Ipswich Town at Etihad Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images) Toure is not concerned by the recent form of Italy international goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma. “Gigio is a fantastic person,” he said. Maybe he’s going through a tough period, but he’s an exemplary professional and knows exactly what he needs to do to return to his best level. And I’m sure he will because he’s one of the best goalkeepers in the world.”

item.title: The line between sports hero and gambling shill is fast disappearing
item.description: LeBron James will make $15m a year from his deal with Polymarket. Photograph: Matt Slocum/AP When Giannis Antetokounmpo announced he was taking an investment stake in prediction market Kalshi in February, the claim he made to accompany the announcement – “We all on Kalshi now” – sounded as absurd as the howls of outrage from sports lovers seemed universal. Nine months later, Kalshi’s grip on American fans appears murderously tight: notional monthly trading volume on the platform, the majority of which is taken up by wagers on sports, increased to nearly $100bn in October from $40bn in August, as the company gears up for yet another funding round at a rumored valuation of $65bn ahead of a potential IPO. Rival prediction market Polymarket, which relaunched in the US late last year after regulators shut it down in 2022, has seen similar growth over recent months. However righteous the disgust from fans on social media at the deepening incursion of these odious platforms into professional sport may be, their popularity seems only to grow. More perplexing is the widening circle of athletes like Giannis who’ve thrown off whatever shame might once have come from association with these businesses and given them their full-throated support. The line between role model and shill in professional sports is now essentially non-existent. Pete Sampras, a man so private in retirement it can often seem like his entire tennis career was a collective hallucination, released an ad for Kalshi during this year’s US Open after two decades largely out of the public eye. José Mourinho trousered a brick of Kalshi cash this summer in exchange for a gambling promo during the World Cup. The prediction market machine now sponsors Jalen Brunson and Josh Hart’s Roommates Show, on which the recently crowned pair of NBA champions begin every episode dutifully informing us that their amazingly dreary podcast is “presented by Polymarket, the top prediction market”. LeBron James will make more from his recently announced partnership with Polymarket – $15m a year – than he will from playing for the Philadelphia 76ers. Somehow we’ve arrived at the point where it’s bigger news if a professional athlete takes a firm stand against the prediction markets, as Victor Wembanyama recently did , rather than pockets the cash to endorse them. Related: Victor Wembanyama said no to gambling money. In today’s NBA, that feels radical Giannis, Sampras, Mourinho, LeBron: these are all wealthy individuals with giant reputations to protect. What exactly is going on here? Surely whatever money is on offer from these platforms is functionally immaterial to these men’s bank balances; surely the predicticoin is not worth the cultural damage that comes from being associated with an industry that’s seen as a symptom of professional sport’s moral rot. Or is it? Is the money really too good to refuse? Has the contest for attention in modern sport and culture become so furious that even famed recluses like Sampr
item.content:encoded: LeBron James will make $15m a year from his deal with Polymarket. Photograph: Matt Slocum/AP When Giannis Antetokounmpo announced he was taking an investment stake in prediction market Kalshi in February, the claim he made to accompany the announcement – “We all on Kalshi now” – sounded as absurd as the howls of outrage from sports lovers seemed universal. Nine months later, Kalshi’s grip on American fans appears murderously tight: notional monthly trading volume on the platform, the majority of which is taken up by wagers on sports, increased to nearly $100bn in October from $40bn in August, as the company gears up for yet another funding round at a rumored valuation of $65bn ahead of a potential IPO. Rival prediction market Polymarket, which relaunched in the US late last year after regulators shut it down in 2022, has seen similar growth over recent months. However righteous the disgust from fans on social media at the deepening incursion of these odious platforms into professional sport may be, their popularity seems only to grow. More perplexing is the widening circle of athletes like Giannis who’ve thrown off whatever shame might once have come from association with these businesses and given them their full-throated support. The line between role model and shill in professional sports is now essentially non-existent. Pete Sampras, a man so private in retirement it can often seem like his entire tennis career was a collective hallucination, released an ad for Kalshi during this year’s US Open after two decades largely out of the public eye. José Mourinho trousered a brick of Kalshi cash this summer in exchange for a gambling promo during the World Cup. The prediction market machine now sponsors Jalen Brunson and Josh Hart’s Roommates Show, on which the recently crowned pair of NBA champions begin every episode dutifully informing us that their amazingly dreary podcast is “presented by Polymarket, the top prediction market”. LeBron James will make more from his recently announced partnership with Polymarket – $15m a year – than he will from playing for the Philadelphia 76ers. Somehow we’ve arrived at the point where it’s bigger news if a professional athlete takes a firm stand against the prediction markets, as Victor Wembanyama recently did , rather than pockets the cash to endorse them. Related: Victor Wembanyama said no to gambling money. In today’s NBA, that feels radical Giannis, Sampras, Mourinho, LeBron: these are all wealthy individuals with giant reputations to protect. What exactly is going on here? Surely whatever money is on offer from these platforms is functionally immaterial to these men’s bank balances; surely the predicticoin is not worth the cultural damage that comes from being associated with an industry that’s seen as a symptom of professional sport’s moral rot. Or is it? Is the money really too good to refuse? Has the contest for attention in modern sport and culture become so furious that even famed recluses like Sampras are suddenly gripped by a desperation to be maximally visible and “relevant”? Is the whole infrastructure of sport now so thoroughly poisoned by gambling and speculation thatthe stain that might once have come from taking money off such businesses has been cleaned? Perhaps it’s a bit of all three. Kalshi and Polymarket, ravenous for any shred of positive exposure and racing toward public offerings before the bottom falls out of the stock market, are deploying vast sums of money in a bewildering variety of directions to get on the American public’s good side. Every writer in US media today has heard stories of journalists being offered tens of thousands of dollars for even the most anodyne forms of engagement (replies, likes) with the online output of the prediction markets. Even for a billionaire like LeBron, a $15m annual pay packet is probably hard to resist. But it’s also important to put these grubby little partnerships between already-wealthy athletes and the prediction markets into their proper cultural context: the Kalshi dollars are raining down on the expensively polished heads of the sporting plutocrats at a time of collective obsession, not only in sports but across culture, with “getting this bread”. You only have to listen to Magic Johnson ( estimated net worth: $1.6bn) ruefully reflect on the time he turned down stock in Nike (“Five billion dollars it would have been worth today”) to understand that for the already obscenely wealthy, there is no greater loss than a lost opportunity for more wealth. This is an axiom of American success: once you are rich, it is important to get richer. In basketball, the rule of separation is paramount. Scoring is a game of space; to make room for a shot, a pass, a dribble, it’s critical that offensive players find ways to separate themselves from their defenders. In an increasingly unequal economy, especially one in which the AI doomers all assure us that there are only a few years of productive mass employment left before the machines swallow all the jobs, the need to find separation moves from a law of sport to a law of social self-preservation, and it’s hard not to detect the outlines of a basic instinct for financial survival in the otherwise unfathomable avarice guiding the decision of these wealthy sporting personalities to sell their souls to the prediction markets. If the economic apocalypse is nigh, hoarding wealth – from whatever quarter it comes – starts to look like common sense; it’s a way to guarantee a seat on the lifeboat, to stay an asset-owning winner in a society that will soon be awash with unsalaried and insolvent losers. Meanwhile, for those outside the 1%, economic uncertainty means that the embrace of “risk-on” thinking – and its corollary; the distortion of prudent household economic management into a series of risky, venture capital-style bets – has come to seem like a financial necessity. Going big on Kalshi and Polymarket now takes its place alongside crypto investing, borrowing on margin, and meme stock trading as a favored hosanna of the American mark. The siren call of the prediction markets increasingly makes social and economic sense for both ends of the income distribution. Amid a cost of living crisis, the ongoing stagnation in wages and the insulting weakness of the US social safety net , high-risk speculation is a last resort for those stuck in the lower percentiles, while for those at the top, embracing the prediction dollar is a riskless win. The sports themselves, of course, have done nothing to disincentive gambling’s well-heeled shills from pursuing their own greed and immorality to its logical ends. Only a few years after sports betting was legalized, professional sport in the US is now a full-time hostage of the gambling and prediction industries. Gambling odds and prediction percentages gum up the screen of every US sports broadcast, almost every league has a partnership with a prediction market (most recently the NBA announced a deal with both Kalshi and Polymarket), and the sheer density of branding in stadiums and sports media from the betting and prediction platforms has made it functionally impossible for fans to evade speculation’s cultural reach. The prediction markets have become normalized; they are now seen as an acceptable part of the furniture, a fact of everyday sporting life. In this environment, it’s no wonder the untroubled rich-guy endorsements have begun to flow. The Democrats’ outperformance in the recent midterm elections has raised expectations of a stiffer approach to federal regulation of the prediction platforms after two years in which the Trump-led White House enabled and encouraged their worst excesses. item.title: New Man Utd boss Mauricio Pochettino eyes summer raid on Borussia Dortmund for frustrated 17-year-old USMNT wonderkid
item.description: United States v Peru - International Friendly - Getty Images Sport New Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino is reportedly eyeing a summer raid on Borussia Dortmund for frustrated 17-year-old USMNT wonderkid Mathis Albert. Having previously worked with the highly-rated attacker while coaching the United States, the Argentine could offer him a route to Old Trafford if his limited minutes in Germany continue. Pochettino monitors frustrated Dortmund teenager According to Sky Germany , Pochettino could push United to sign Albert amid his lack of regular action at Dortmund. The 17-year-old attacking talent has been restricted to just 128 minutes across three appearances this season, sparking dissatisfaction over his sporting situation. He was handed a rare outing on Saturday, coming off the bench in the 72nd minute of Dortmund's 1-0 win over Borussia Monchengladbach . Argentine admires young American attacker Pochettino knows Albert's qualities well, having nurtured the youngster early on and handed him his senior call-up during his spell as United States head coach. Following his recent appointment at Old Trafford , the connection between the two has gained fresh momentum as the Red Devils plan for the future. The report states that Pochettino remains a big admirer of his former international charge and believes "Albert needs to play" to fulfil his potential. Should the teenager's situation in the Bundesliga fail to improve over the coming months, the Argentine coach could offer him the chance to earn more regular first-team minutes in England. Teenager already broke USMNT record Widely regarded as one of Dortmund's brightest academy prospects, Albert is still waiting for a genuine senior breakthrough in Germany. Across all competitions, he has made four first-team appearances for BVB, with his only start to date coming in the first round of the DFB Cup back in early September. At international level, however, he has already collected five caps for the United States. On September 30, 2026, he netted in a 4-2 win over Chile at 17 years and 131 days old to become the USMNT's youngest-ever goalscorer in just his second outing, though Cavan Sullivan broke that mark four days later against Mexico aged 17 years and six days. Summer window could prove decisive A winter transfer is currently off the table, with the German outlet noting that Albert wants to see how the rest of the campaign unfolds first. He will closely monitor his playing time at Dortmund over the next few months before deciding on his next step. If his frustration persists, Pochettino and United are poised to make a concrete summer move.

item.title: ‘Ick,’ ‘That Body Language Says It All’ — Commanders Fans Take Issue With Ja’Marr Chase’s Assessment of Why Bengals Lost on MNF
item.description: ‘Ick,’ ‘That Body Language Says It All’ — Commanders Fans Take Issue With Ja’Marr Chase’s Assessment of Why Bengals Lost on MNF Ja’Marr Chase and the Cincinnati Bengals entered Monday’s game with a five-game winning streak and were looking to improve their 7-2 record. However, Washington produced a late comeback to secure the 22-20 win. The loss ended Cincinnati’s winning run and dropped the team to 7-3 this season. Chase had been enjoying a magnificent season heading into the MNF matchup, but the Commanders’ defense managed to keep the wide receiver largely quiet. Meanwhile, Chase’s reaction to the Bengals’ loss to the Commanders also earned him jabs from fans. Commanders Fans Question Ja’Marr Chase’s Confidence After Washington Silences Bengals Chase was coming off a phenomenal 231-yard outing against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 10. However, he finished against Washington with just five receptions for 31 yards on nine targets, without a touchdown, ranking No. 2 in PFN’s WR Impact Score with a grade of 96.1 through Week 11. Following the Bengals’ loss and his own underwhelming performance, Chase was asked about the most difficult aspect of coming away from a loss. “Losing when you know you’re better. That’s the worst.” Chase said , according to Mike Petraglia. Commanders fans used the chance to poke fun at Chase. “Ja’Marr Chase has never beaten the Washington Commanders in his entire career, idk what type of pedestal he thinks the Bengals are compared to the Commanders,” a fan said . SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer “0-2 btw… Higgins and Burrow 0-3 vs DC,” one said . “Whew.. that body language says it all,” one added . Washington’s defensive approach also played a significant role in limiting Cincinnati’s offensive production. The Commanders entered the game with one of the highest blitz rates in the NFL and continued to apply pressure to Joe Burrow throughout. The Commanders sacked Burrow three times, while the Bengals receiving duo of Chase and Tee Higgins combined for only seven catches for 74 yards. Commanders fans had reason to challenge Chase’s assessment because Cincinnati has now lost its last three meetings against Washington. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor “ICKKKKK,” another said . “The Bengals ranked 2nd in EPA/play and success rate entering MNF. The marks they achieved on MNF would have the following ranks for the season: EPA/play – 17th, success rate – 28th. Perhaps the better team didn’t hit it’s usual standard against a defense missing three starter,” Grant Mitchell, host of the ‘Full Command Show,’ wrote . “You are 0-2 against us and Burrow is 0-3. Know your place, one added . The Bengals will now look to bounce back when they return home to face the New Orleans Saints in Week 12. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Tuesday ‘Dawg Bites Ain’t Got Time For That
item.description: ATHENS, GA - NOVEMBER 14: University of Georgia mascot UGA XI stands on the field during the college football game between the Missouri Tigers and the University of Georgia Bulldogs on November 14, 2026 at Sanford Stadium in Athens, GA. (Photo by Jeff Robinson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to Tuesday, Bulldog fans! And the last Tuesday of the 2026 regular season. It has certainly flown by, but we’ve no time for reminiscing. Because once again, it is Hate Week. That of the Clean, Old-Fashioned variety. So while folks in College Station and Nashville try to relive the few moments of glory from the quickly ending season, and boards of directors in the bad Columbia and Red Stick fret over the weird December schedule affecting the coaching carousel, we UGA fans still have a lot of football to look forward to. And nothing has changed in the football offices, even this, the week of Thanksgiving. If you think the Dawgs are rounding into form and staying focused, that starts at the top. In Monday’s press conference, head coach Kirby Smart was peaking in his reponses to reporter’s questions. Curt a few times, deflecting a few more, praising his players whenever possible, and telling the assembled that they don’t know how a football program is run. In that vein, if you’ve seen social media posts or interweb headlines touting “What Kirby Smart Said About Glenn Schumann and the FSU Opening”, just breeze right on by. He said two things which can be summed up thusly: Schumann has done a wonderful job at UGA, and UGA is focused on Georgia Tech. Full stop. But you might not ignore the fact that both the school and Schumann himself have released statements on his offer and acceptance of steering the Seminole ship . Not much on the injury front either, as the only update on Center Drew Bobo was he hopes to have him available this week. It didn’t make much noise, but Earnest Greene III earned another SEC Offensive Lineman of the Week Award after having his way with the SC Gamecocks. Not quite as prestigious, the intrepid folks over at the Red & Black decided to put out another position group scorecard after the Pillaging of the Palmetto State. If the lowest grade is given to the wide receivers, you know it was a good night for the Bulldogs. There’s all kinds of other stories out there, like Lane Kiffin apologizing and throwing his roster under the bus, Kyle Whittingham continuing to coach for the buyout, UCLA reading the playbook on how to falsely reassure the CFP committee all is well, and another meeting next week to decide if LSU should remain in the Southeastern Conference. So, just another Tuesday. Safe travels to everyone out there, and safe food handling to all the others. Enjoy your Tuesday, and as always… GO ‘DAWGS!!!

item.title: MiLaysia Fulwiley Treated to Big Ovation From LSU Fans as Lady Tigers Star Hits 1,500 Career Points in Return After Arrest
item.description: MiLaysia Fulwiley ©IMAGO/Newscom World After piling up 17 steals and 11 blocks across her first four games, MiLaysia Fulwiley spent two outings on the sideline while unbeaten LSU rolled on without her. Nine days after her arrest in Baton Rouge, another question surrounded the senior guard’s return to the Pete Maravich Assembly Center against Belmont: How would LSU fans respond? Once she stepped back onto the floor, Monday night delivered far more than an ordinary return to the rotation. During LSU’s home matchup against Belmont on November 23, 2026, in Baton Rouge, Fulwiley checked in off the bench with 4:37 remaining in the first quarter and the Tigers already ahead 13–0. Covering the game courtside for the USA TODAY Network, reporter Cory Diaz documented the crowd’s response on X as MiLaysia Fulwiley made her first appearance in 10 days: “MiLaysia Fulwiley gets a big ovation from the #LSU fans here in the PMAC.” The warm welcome captured in Cory Diaz’s X post opened a productive night for Fulwiley, who returned from her two-game absence following a November 14 arrest to finish with 14 points, five steals, and 1,500 career points in LSU’s 103–45 win over Belmont. Later in the fourth quarter, with 1:35 remaining and LSU up 100–42, the arena video board honored the scoring milestone in a separate moment shared on X by reporter Andre Champagne. From the bench, MiLaysia Fulwiley waved and flashed a hand heart toward the cheering crowd while teammates celebrated around her. A comeback moment and a historic milestone converge as MiLaysia Fulwiley reclaims her place on LSU's biggest stage. Subscribe for the latest on college basketball's most compelling stories. What MiLaysia Fulwiley’s Return Means for LSU After Two Games Out The night closed a turbulent stretch that began on November 14, when Fulwiley was arrested following a traffic-control encounter with police after LSU’s football game against Texas. Authorities initially booked her on two felony counts—aggravated battery and aggravated assault with a dangerous weapon—alongside three misdemeanor counts related to fleeing, resisting, and disobeying officers over alleged conduct during the stop. While the situation remained under review, she sat out LSU’s home wins over Troy on November 16 and Fairleigh Dickinson on November 19. Her path back opened on November 20, when East Baton Rouge Parish prosecutors dismissed both felony charges while referring the three misdemeanor counts to a pretrial diversion program rather than dismissing every matter outright. item.content:encoded: MiLaysia Fulwiley ©IMAGO/Newscom World After piling up 17 steals and 11 blocks across her first four games, MiLaysia Fulwiley spent two outings on the sideline while unbeaten LSU rolled on without her. Nine days after her arrest in Baton Rouge, another question surrounded the senior guard’s return to the Pete Maravich Assembly Center against Belmont: How would LSU fans respond? Once she stepped back onto the floor, Monday night delivered far more than an ordinary return to the rotation. During LSU’s home matchup against Belmont on November 23, 2026, in Baton Rouge, Fulwiley checked in off the bench with 4:37 remaining in the first quarter and the Tigers already ahead 13–0. Covering the game courtside for the USA TODAY Network, reporter Cory Diaz documented the crowd’s response on X as MiLaysia Fulwiley made her first appearance in 10 days: “MiLaysia Fulwiley gets a big ovation from the #LSU fans here in the PMAC.” The warm welcome captured in Cory Diaz’s X post opened a productive night for Fulwiley, who returned from her two-game absence following a November 14 arrest to finish with 14 points, five steals, and 1,500 career points in LSU’s 103–45 win over Belmont. Later in the fourth quarter, with 1:35 remaining and LSU up 100–42, the arena video board honored the scoring milestone in a separate moment shared on X by reporter Andre Champagne. From the bench, MiLaysia Fulwiley waved and flashed a hand heart toward the cheering crowd while teammates celebrated around her. A comeback moment and a historic milestone converge as MiLaysia Fulwiley reclaims her place on LSU's biggest stage. Subscribe for the latest on college basketball's most compelling stories. What MiLaysia Fulwiley’s Return Means for LSU After Two Games Out The night closed a turbulent stretch that began on November 14, when Fulwiley was arrested following a traffic-control encounter with police after LSU’s football game against Texas. Authorities initially booked her on two felony counts—aggravated battery and aggravated assault with a dangerous weapon—alongside three misdemeanor counts related to fleeing, resisting, and disobeying officers over alleged conduct during the stop. While the situation remained under review, she sat out LSU’s home wins over Troy on November 16 and Fairleigh Dickinson on November 19. Her path back opened on November 20, when East Baton Rouge Parish prosecutors dismissed both felony charges while referring the three misdemeanor counts to a pretrial diversion program rather than dismissing every matter outright. That same day, Fulwiley issued an apology through LSU acknowledging the night never should have happened and that her posts afterward made matters worse, apologizing to the officers, her family, and Tiger fans while focusing on earning back trust. Following a reported return to practice on November 21, LSU confirmed her availability ahead of Belmont . Coming off the bench after starting her first four games, Fulwiley needed less than a minute to make her presence felt by sinking a wing three-pointer on her first shot attempt. Across 17 minutes, she finished 6-of-13 from the field and 2-of-4 from beyond the arc while adding five steals, three blocks, three assists, and a rebound. Through five appearances in 2026–27, MiLaysia Fulwiley is now averaging 17.0 points, 4.4 steals, 4.0 assists, and 2.8 blocks. Her 14 points against Belmont carried added weight because they pushed her career scoring total to 1,500. Combining 904 points across two seasons at South Carolina, 511 points at LSU in 2025–26, and 71 points over her first four games this season—capped by 23 against Denver on November 13—she entered Monday sitting at 1,486. Remarkably, the milestone arrived almost exactly a year after LSU Athletics documented her crossing 1,000 career points with 18 points in a 112–49 win over Alcorn State on November 20, 2025. That scoring pace underscores why her reintegration matters so much to Kim Mulkey’s lineup. In her first season in Baton Rouge in 2025–26, MiLaysia Fulwiley led the Tigers with 511 points—averaging 14.6 per game—and captured her second straight SEC Sixth Woman of the Year award after winning a national championship at South Carolina in 2024. Bringing that proven perimeter scoring and defensive disruption back off the bench deepens an already dangerous roster. Still, Monday’s 58-point blowout was far from a one-player effort. LSU raced to a 22–0 opening run before Belmont scored with 17 seconds left in the first quarter, cruising to 7–0 while holding a sixth opponent in seven games under 50 points. Senior guard Mikaylah Williams paced the Tigers with 20 points and 10 assists, and all 11 LSU players who appeared reached the scoring column. Unbeaten LSU now heads away from Baton Rouge for the first time this season, facing Villanova on November 27 and NC State on November 28 at the neutral-site Fort Myers Tip-Off. Monday’s warm PMAC reception and 1,500-point milestone gave MiLaysia Fulwiley an immediate on-court reset in the rotation, while her remaining misdemeanor charges had been referred to diversion. item.title: Enzo Maresca has said Abdukodir Khusanov is better suited to centre-back than right-back as Manchester City weigh up their options ahead of the 2027 January transfer window.
item.description: Enzo Maresca has said Abdukodir Khusanov is better suited to centre-back than right-back as Manchester City weigh up their options ahead of the 2027 January transfer window. Right-back has been area of concern for Manchester City's leaky defence of late. More Videos Maresca has used Matheus Nunes as his first-choice right-back this season and the Portugal international is back in contention after an ankle problem kept him out of Saturday's 1-1 draw with Fulham . Abdukodir Khusanov started at right-back in Nunes' absence against Fulham, with Rodrigo Muniz getting the better of the Uzbekistan international for the opening goal before Elliot Anderson volleyed in a second-half equaliser. Maresca discusses Man City's right-back prospects ahead of Napoli test Speaking in a press conference ahead of Tuesday's UEFA Champions League clash with Napoli, Maresca discussed his options at right-back following strong criticism aimed at the Blues' backline after a poor run of Premier League results. The Manchester City manager said: "Since we started, we've used Rico [Lewis] there, but also [Abdukodir] Khusa, that I think he can play there. For sure, it's much better - I'm trying to find the right balance. "If you ask me if Khusa [Khusanov] is a better right-back or central defender, no doubt: Central defender. I know that. But it's a matter of the game, the players we have available. "But Matheus [Nunes] has done very good since we started, the games he has played, overall he was very good." City have been linked with Villarreal right-back Alex Freeman ahead of the January window, with sporting director Hugo Viana having overseen a major squad overhaul since Maresca's arrival in June. Freeman, a 22-year-old United States international who joined Villarreal from Orlando City in January, is said to be open to a move to the Etihad Stadium - and he can also play at centre-back. Maresca also pointed out on Monday that City had conceded seven goals from chances worth around three expected goals across their four-game winless run in the Premier League. It's just a matter of getting to know each other, says Maresca on Man City squad ahead of January window Maresca then explained that he is still getting to know his players, having witnessed a significant overhaul of the first-team dressing room since he replaced Pep Guardiola at the helm in June. "It's just a matter to know each other, I need to understand how is the idea one for these kind of games, the idea one for different kinds of games," the 46-year-old added. "I don't think it's just [the] midfield, also we are trying with defensive players to find the right solution. Again, it's for me part of the process because it's like a reset, a restart, after 10 years with the same manager, same face, same words, same method. "It's not easy to all of sudden change. For me personally, it's all normal, and hopefully as soon as possible we can find the right balance in all the lines - defensive, midfield - and we can be cons

"It's just a matter to know each other, I need to understand how is the idea one for these kind of games, the idea one for different kinds of games," the 46-year-old added. "I don't think it's just [the] midfield, also we are trying with defensive players to find the right solution. Again, it's for me part of the process because it's like a reset, a restart, after 10 years with the same manager, same face, same words, same method. "It's not easy to all of sudden change. For me personally, it's all normal, and hopefully as soon as possible we can find the right balance in all the lines - defensive, midfield - and we can be consistent, which for me is the difference between us and other clubs." Manchester City have lacked a specialist right-back since Kyle Walker left for AC Milan in January 2025, and Nunes has made the position his own despite being a natural central midfielder, with the club reported to be close to agreeing a new contract amid interest from Real Madrid . Liam Delap's second goal in the 3-1 defeat at the City Ground came after the Forest striker flicked the ball past Anderson and Nunes before exchanging passes with Morgan Gibbs-White and finding the far post. Rico Lewis, who turned 22 last week, has filled in at right-back since breaking into the senior squad under Guardiola in 2022, but has said he would prefer to play in midfield , where he feels he can best contribute goals and assists for the team. City go into Tuesday's game against Napoli seventh of 36 in the Champions League league phase, with a top-eight finish guaranteeing direct qualification for the round of 16 and avoiding a February play-off.

item.title: Relief for Arsenal as Raya has not suffered a serious injury
item.description: Relief for Arsenal as Raya has not suffered a serious injury Arsenal have received a major boost after David Raya’s injury proved less serious than initially feared, with the goalkeeper potentially returning to action this weekend. The Spaniard was forced off against Newcastle United after suffering a suspected shoulder injury , leaving the club concerned about his availability for upcoming matches. Raya appeared to be in considerable discomfort following the incident and did not look comfortable as he made his way off the pitch. His reaction immediately raised concerns among Arsenal supporters, who feared the goalkeeper could face a lengthy spell on the sidelines. The club arranged for him to undergo scans after the match to establish the extent of the problem. Fortunately, the results did not reveal any serious damage, giving Arsenal encouragement that their first-choice goalkeeper could return much sooner than expected. Arteta provides encouraging injury update Raya is one of Arsenal’s most important players and has established himself as one of the leading goalkeepers in world football. Losing him for an extended period would have been a significant setback for Mikel Arteta’s side as they look to build on their success from last season. However, the latest assessment suggests the situation is not as concerning as it initially appeared. Raya will miss the Borussia Dortmund match, but there is now hope that he could be available again at the weekend. Speaking to Arsenal Media ahead of the Champions League fixture, Arteta provided an update on the goalkeeper’s condition and explained why the initial reaction had been worrying. He said: “He’s not fit for tomorrow unfortunately, but it doesn’t look too serious. We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. “With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action, we were all quite worried, but he seems to be better than we expected. When you look at the action, it doesn’t seem to be much on it, but the extent of the pain that he had and how he was struggling, it was quite worrying.” (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) Arsenal hope Raya returns quickly The Gunners will continue monitoring Raya before deciding when he can return. His availability would be a welcome boost, particularly with important fixtures approaching. Although Arsenal must manage without him against Dortmund, Arteta will be encouraged by the progress so far. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. You agree not to give any personal abuse to other Arsenal fans. Everyone is allowed to hold their own opinions even if you disagree with them. It COSTS NOTHING TO BE POLITE TO OTHER ARSENAL FANS. item.title: PhHN Daily: Flyers Trade Talk; Ripple Effect from the Dylan Larkin Deal
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to the 11/24 edition of the PhHN Daily. Starting with the Flyers, we have some trade talk. First, we look at the fallout of the Dylan Larkin trade, then discuss how it could impact the Flyers’ pursuit of another disgruntled Red Wing, and if it becomes a more realistic possibility now more than ever. We also have some more Flyers trade rumors to keep an eye on. Around the league, you guessed it, more Larkin fallout! Even though there was a direct impact on two teams, the effect rippled to more than just the Red Wings and Canadiens. On the 11/24 edition of the PhHN Daily, we explore the other impacts of the trade. Get all of that & more on the 11/24 edition of the PhHN Daily! Philadelphia Flyers Philly Hockey Now: The Detroit Red Wings have finally moved on from Dylan Larkin. That should begin the opening of the floodgates of trade season. In our latest Flyers’ trade talk, we explore how the Larkin trade could make the Flyers’ pursuit of Red Wing defenseman Simon Edvinsson more realistic . Dave Pagnotta: We all know the Flyers search to upgrade at center is ongoing. That’s not the only position that they’re looking at adding at. The Flyers still need a young top-pair defenseman to build for the future alongside Oliver Bonk . Dave Pagnotta reports that the Flyers have ongoing interest in Simon Edvinsson and Alexander Nikishin . David Pagnotta: Philadelphia's been a team that's been looking to rejig the blueline a little bit and upgrade, which is why they've had interest in Alexander Nikishin in the past; they've had interest in Simon Edvinsson – DFO Insider (11/19) — NHL Rumour Report (@NHLRumourReport) November 24, 2026 Tony Escargot: A few Dailys back, we mentioned how anonymous Flyers fan Tony Escargot started a GoFundMe for a banner plane and billboard to share his frustrations with the team. item.title: ‘One of us’ – NFL fans praise Pat McAfee after hilarious reaction to Jason Kelce on MNF
item.description: Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images ESPN’s Monday Night Football coverage has taken a lot of criticism this season, with Joe Buck and Troy Aikman’s saga being one of the big talking points. However, ESPN’s pre-game show and alt cast, including the controversial Pat McAfee, have also proven incredibly divisive. Despite a lot of fans having vented their frustrations with McAfee throughout the season, a lot of people loved what they saw him doing during this week’s show. Jason Kelce has also split the opinions of the viewers on ESPN, which left many fans on Monday night enjoying McAfee not paying any attention at all to the former Philadelphia Eagles centre. NFL fans provide rare praise towards Pat McAfee during Monday Night Football McAfee has been pushed considerably by ESPN over a number of different programmes, with the former Indianapolis Colts punter being made to earn every cent he is being paid by the network. ‘Pat McAfee isn’t even listening to Jason Kelce. One of us!’ one fan said on X during the pre-game show on Monday Night Football. Another fan replied: ‘And why would u? Jason Kelce just commented that Jayden Daniels has been so flawless in two-minute & end-of-game scenarios this season.’ It is rare to see McAfee earn the praise of the viewers, with many still feeling as if he is being given way too much airtime by ESPN. Alongside his own show during the week, McAfee is also presenting College Gameday and the Monday Night Football alt cast. ‘For 2027, ESPN should make its MNF broadcasters Joe Buck and Pat McAfee,’ said another NFL fan. McAfee has been known for being incredibly charitable, and alongside the NFL, he is now giving away Super Bowl tickets in a pre-game kickoff catch game. This is a feature which has also gone down extremely well with viewers on ESPN. ‘Don’t love his show, but Pat McAfee is changing folks’ lives weekly. I do appreciate that,’ one fan said on X. McAfee also made a $25,000 donation to The GR8 Chase charity ahead of kickoff as a result of the kickoff catch competition, which provided the fan with tickets to the Super Bowl at SoFi Stadium. ‘Pat McAfee gives away MILLIONS to charity,’ replied another. Read more: Fans convinced Troy Aikman wants ESPN to fire him after ‘hilariously awful’ NFL Primetime comments Chris Long names the ‘most underrated player in the NFL’ right now who is doing ‘a great job’ Mike LaFleur sends clear message after Cardinals fire DC following Chiefs blowout

item.title: Accused of ‘emptying the coffers’, Macron mulls spending caps for future French governments
item.description: Right-wing candidates vying to succeed French President Emmanuel Macron have welcomed his suggestion of a “golden rule” to cap government spending and keep deficits in check, even as they mock the profligacy of his decade in power. Critics of the proposal denounce a budgetary straitjacket imposed on future governments and a distraction from the president’s growing impotence at home.

item.title: InferNode gives Bell Labs' Inferno OS a 64-bit second wind
item.description: InferNode brings a modernized, 64-bit edition of Inferno, the distributed operating system that followed Plan 9 from Bell Labs. For us, the strapline of the InferNode project distracts from the interesting part. It describes the project as a "Secure Runtime for AI Agents," but we think it's something far more interesting than another LLM tool. Fair warning: this vulture has no interest whatsoever in AI agents, and we are not even going to look at this planned use of InferNode. We're interested in the OS, and here, its GitHub repository spells out the part that caught our attention: "a 64-bit Inferno® OS." That grabbed us because Inferno is a very interesting OS, although it doesn't get much attention – for example, the official Inferno GitHub repository shows little activity in the last few years. Inferno is the successor to Plan 9, which we've written and talked about before , including recent releases of its community continuation, 9front . Plan 9 is what the team who invented Unix did next. Plan 9 is a very minimalist, natively clustered Unix: machines can freely mount one another's filesystems, display windows on one another, and start processes on one another. Plan 9 turns a network of machines running this Unix-like OS into a single machine. So, for instance, if you were working on a laptop with limited storage and compute power, you could compile a large complex project on a faster machine elsewhere on the network, using project files located on a third machine, while watching the process in your terminal on your screen, with no messing about with SSH sessions. Plan 9 and 9front programs are compiled into architecture-specific native binaries. Different processor families can still work together across the network, but the same executable won't run unchanged on both an x86-64 laptop and an Arm64 server. Inferno takes a different approach. It's contemporaneous with the far less ambitious Java. On Inferno, languages compile code for a VM called Dis, which is part of the kernel. This means that Inferno binaries execute directly on anything that the Inferno kernel runs on. The OS kernel is built to run bare-metal, or as a process on various other OSes, without needing a separate hardware virtual machine or hypervisor. A single binary can run on all supported CPU architectures. Inferno applications are normally written in the Limbo programming language , whose documentation was written by Unix co-creator Dennis Ritchie. Limbo is one of the languages that influenced Go, but Inferno lets compilers for other languages target Dis as well. The binaries run anywhere. Inferno on Arm, or x86, or RISC-V, or running in a Windows or Linux or macOS process, your program just runs. We've been trying to contact Vita Nuova , the company that maintains Inferno, for some years without success. Development appears to have slowed considerably.
